question: Alloys, air, lemonade, and soda water are examples of which of the following categories of solutions?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Homogeneous mixture**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• A **homogeneous mixture** is a type of mixture where the **components** are distributed **uniformly** throughout the entire volume, and there are no visible boundaries of separation between the constituents.
 
• **Alloys** are considered **homogeneous mixtures** of **metals** (or a metal and a non-metal) because they show the properties of their constituents and can have variable compositions, yet they cannot be separated into their components by simple physical methods. An example is **Brass**, which contains approximately **30% Zinc** and **70% Copper**.
 
• **Air** is a **homogeneous mixture** of various **gases**. Its main components are **Nitrogen (78%)** and **Oxygen (21%)**, with smaller amounts of **Argon**, **Carbon dioxide**, and water vapor distributed evenly.
